idiom_name: java.util.logging.Handler (or a SLF4J/Logback appender) with a chained javax.crypto.Mac
implementation_notes: java.util.logging gives the chokepoint in the standard library: extend Handler, implement publish(LogRecord), flush() and close(), canonicalise the record, and chain an HmacSHA256 Mac tag into a file opened in append mode; Logback or Log4j2 appenders are the equivalent when they are already in the stack, and javax.crypto.Mac is the same either way. The classic hand-written writer is justified mainly when the audit stream must bypass the logging framework entirely - for example an audit row written inside the same transaction as the business change - so that a lost log call cannot be masked by an asynchronous appender.
pitfalls: Handler.publish is invoked on the logging thread and may be re-entered from several threads (or async appenders): synchronise the chain state or funnel it through a single writer, otherwise sequence numbers interleave.
Message parameters, suppliers and exceptions can carry secrets and CRLF - canonicalise and redact inside the handler, and never treat a log message as a format string.
Mac.clone() throws CloneNotSupportedException and a prepared Mac shared across threads mutates: pick one (clone per record, or a ThreadLocal) deliberately, and keep the key out of the log store.
